chief_complaint: preoccupation with having pancreatic cancer, normal scans
hpi_details: A 71-year-old male presents to the clinic with preoccupation with having pancreatic cancer, normal scans. The patient states the symptoms started recently and have been gradually worsening, accompanied by generalized fatigue.
ideas: He thinks his mild abdominal twinges and fatigue mean he is developing pancreatic cancer, just like a close friend whose tumor was missed on early tests.
concerns: He is worried that delaying advanced testing will allow an undetectable tumor to spread past the point of being operable.
expectations: He hopes to receive a referral for an endoscopic ultrasound or a PET scan to definitively prove his pancreas is clear.

history.answer: I have been terrified that I have pancreatic cancer, Doctor, even though my doctor told me my recent scans were completely clear.
My worry is entirely focused on my physical health and the fear of having an undetected pancreatic tumor. I don't really fret about money, family conflicts, or daily routine matters.
This started about seven months ago, right after a close friend passed away from cancer, and the fear has been gradually getting worse.
I'm terrified that while everyone tells me I'm fine, a tumor is growing silently and will become inoperable before we catch it.
No, I haven't had sudden heart pounding, gasping for breath, chest tightness, or a sudden fear that I'm going to drop dead on the spot.
I don't avoid crowds, public transport, or open spaces, but I do feel intense dread whenever I walk into a clinic or hospital.
No, I have no fear of talking in front of other people or being watched and judged at gatherings.
I feel constantly exhausted and my neck muscles feel tight and achy. I also toss and turn for hours before falling asleep because my mind keeps racing with cancer thoughts.
It has completely taken over my daily life. I spend hours glued to my computer reading about survival rates instead of doing my hobbies or enjoying time with my family.
Seven months ago, a good friend from my weekly club was suddenly diagnosed with advanced pancreatic cancer and died within weeks. That hit me extremely hard.
I don't have flashbacks or nightmares about trauma, but I do get repetitive, nagging thoughts about cancer that I just can't shake out of my head.
I feel quite down and worn out because of this non-stop fear, but I have never thought about ending my life or hurting myself.
No fever, no unexpected weight loss, and no excessive sweating or heat intolerance. My weight has stayed steady all year.
No, I don't get chest pain or shortness of breath when I walk up hills, and I have never fainted.
I don't have severe stomach pain or back pain, maybe just a little bloating or stomach awareness now and then, which immediately makes me think the worst.

Two months ago, I had an ultrasound and a contrast abdominal CT done at another hospital, and both were normal. The doctors told me I'm fine, but I keep worrying that they missed a tiny, deadly tumor.
I check the whites of my eyes in the mirror multiple times a day for jaundice, inspect my stool every time I use the restroom, and search online symptoms for hours.
I'm terrified that while everyone tells me I'm fine, a tumor is growing silently and will become inoperable before we catch it.

history.answer: I only drink one mug of mild black coffee in the morning. I never drink energy drinks or take caffeine pills.
I don't take sleeping pills, sedatives, or any tranquilizers, and I have never used illicit drugs.
I try taking long walks to clear my head, but as soon as I sit down, the worry comes rushing back. My previous doctor suggested talking to someone, but I felt I needed another scan first.
history.topic: Coping efforts and past doctor visits

history.answer: I'm convinced that these deep twinges in my belly mean I have pancreatic cancer, especially since my close friend's scans were clean until it was too late.
I'm terrified that while everyone tells me I'm fine, a tumor is growing silently and will become inoperable before we catch it.
I want an endoscopic ultrasound or a PET scan today so we can be 100% certain there is nothing hiding in there.
I have no chronic medical conditions, no high blood pressure, no diabetes, and no history of liver disease.
I had my appendix removed when I was twenty-two, but no other surgeries or hospitalizations since then.
I am not taking any prescription medications, over-the-counter pain relievers, or herbal supplements.
I have no allergies to medications, foods, or CT contrast dye.
I have never smoked cigarettes or used tobacco in my life.
I only have half a glass of beer or wine once or twice a month at social dinners.
I am a retired high school teacher and live comfortably at home with my wife.
There is no family history of pancreatic cancer, gastrointestinal malignancies, or anxiety disorders.

Patient is a well-groomed older gentleman who appears mildly anxious and preoccupied, but is in no acute physical distress.
Alert and fully oriented to person, place, and time; speech is coherent and goal-directed, thought process is organized, and mood is noticeably anxious without psychotic features.
Sclerae are white and non-icteric, and palpebral conjunctivae are pink with no pallor.
Pupils are equal, round, and reactive to light; extraocular movements are intact with no lid lag or exophthalmos.
Thyroid gland is normal in size, smooth, and non-tender, with no palpable nodules or bruits.
No postural or resting tremor is observed in the outstretched hands.
Heart sounds S1 and S2 are normal and regular, with no murmurs, gallops, or friction rubs.
Clear breath sounds bilaterally throughout all lung fields without wheezes, crackles, or rhonchi.
Abdomen is flat and symmetric with a well-healed right lower quadrant surgical scar; no visible distension, jaundice, or abnormal vascular markings.
Abdomen is soft and non-tender to light and deep palpation across all four quadrants including the epigastrium, without guarding or rigidity.
Liver and spleen are not palpable below the costal margins, with no organomegaly or tenderness.
No skin jaundice, spider angiomas, palmar erythema, excoriations, or rashes are present.
